routes.label: applied for through the DNR's portal or office

note: The State Minister responsible for the DNR, to Parliament's Committee on National Development and Heritage, as Edition.mv reported: a card for a person aged 10 to 40 is valid five years, an older person's ten; a permanent card from 65 was being prepared (not modelled). The fee is on the DNR's application form, which wasn't reached (the missions' pages refused this session), so it's null; so is the time. 40 itself is kept with the older. Tried again 2026-10-29: the missions' pages say the fee is paid to the Department in Malé or through the High Commission, without the amount. Tried again 2026-10-30: a search for the fee in rufiyaa found the missions' FAQs (fees on the DNR form; a fine of 100 to 200 for a damaged card, not modelled), Edition.mv and the Fuvahmulah City Council's guide (a fee link is sent after the DNR checks the application), none with the card's amount.

sources.title: Edition.mv, on the DNR's plan for permanent identity cards from 65
sources.said: responded that the validity of identity cards for persons aged between 10 and 40 is five years, while those older receive a card with 10 year validity.
